point1_overSizeMappingMessages.againstS3: S3 measured 45,161 and 44,648 characters; the same tables measure 438 more on this base. The cause was not looked for.
point1_overSizeMappingMessages.finding: Taking every sample value away does not bring either table within any of the gateway's bounds. With no samples the user message is 33,178 and 33,054 characters against 32,768 (over by 410 and 286), and the two messages together, as built, are 37,690 and 37,566 bytes against 24,576 (over by 13,114 and 12,990). Samples are 28% of the message; the value shapes are 39%.
point1_overSizeMappingMessages.whatMustShrink: to pass the 24,576-byte bound each table must lose about 13,100 bytes beyond its samples. Only the value shapes (17,717 and 17,655) are large enough; headers, the vocabulary and the column structure are fixed by the decisions. The other way is two requests of 45 columns each, which drops no column but is not the decided rule.
point1_overSizeMappingMessages.whoTheRuleHelps: by these sizes a table costs about 307 bytes a column with no samples and about 447 with ten, beside 693 + 5,356 of fixed text. The rule can bring within the bound a table of roughly 42 to 59 columns (an estimate from these two tables); a wider one is refused with no samples. Of the 50 development mapping requests, S3 found 2 refused (these two); none is in the range the rule helps.
